$Comment: The Mastery Trainer, standing in the Forgotten Temple across from the Adventurer's Guide.
This pack's copy of the trainer's placement: same standing, same look, but pressing F opens
the Mmo_Mastery_Trainer conversation instead of the bare mastery screen, because with this
pack installed the trainer has quests to hand out - the conversation offers the quest list,
the mastery menu, and a farewell. This file wins over the one in the mod jar by pack rank;
delete it (or set Enabled false in mods/ziggfreedcommon/npc-placements.json) to fall back.
Where targets the temple by its GameplayConfig key rather than by name: that key is the
engine's own per-world gameplay-config id - 'ForgottenTemple' ships with the base game - and
it is the same every time the temple is entered, while the world NAME carries a fresh uuid
Requires keeps the trainer away until the mastery feature is switched on; Lifecycle keeps
their chunk loaded, puts them back if something removes them, and raises their health beyond
anything that can be dealt. This placement authors no Identity.NpcId, so the character IS its
role: the pack's mastery quests bind to Mmo_Mastery_Trainer, and any second placement of that
role is the same trainer, offering and taking hand-ins for the same quests.
Name: Mmo_Mastery_Trainer_Temple
